To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the surface treatment of ZnO nanomaterials is essential to achieving their full piezoelectric potential.
the piezocoefficients of ZnO nanorods are reduced due to the surface effects and the surface effects are dependent on the surface treatment and the nanorod orientation.

if appropriate surface passivation is utilized to eliminate surface polarization divergence, then (i) the piezoelectricty of ZnO nanorods is reduced as compared to bulk values, (ii) the reduction in effective piezoconstant is not related to the surface stress, but is related to the bond length of Zn–O dipoles closest to the (0001) polar surface and (iii) continued miniaturization will not result in enhanced piezoelectric behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how surface effects influence the piezoelectrical properties of ZnO nanostructures.
understanding and predicting the piezoelectricty of ZnO nanoscale wires as a function of their axial orientation, size and surface treatment.
the effects of surface treatments on the piezoproperties of ZnO nanomaterials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
if one desires to utilize piezoelectric nanowires in a device application, then one must be aware of the surface treatment of these nanowires.

the surface effects of the polar surfaces of wurtzite ZnO nanowire are detrimental to the piezoelectrics of the nanowire, and that surface treatments to eliminate the polarization discontinuity across the surface are required to achieve the desired piezoelectric enhancement.
surface treatment of ZnO nanoscale wires can reduce the piezoelectrical properties, but not necessarily increase them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the surface effects of the polar (0011) surfaces of the ZnO nanowire must be taken into consideration in order to accurately predict the piezoelectrical properties of the ZnO nanostructure.
if one is interested in utilizing the piezoelectrical properties of ZnO, then the surface effects must be considered and the surface must be appropriately treated.
if the piezoelectrical properties are to be improved for ZnO, then surface treatments must be utilized to eliminate the polarization divergences that occur at the polar surfaces of the wurtzitic ZnO.
The main takeaway from our work is that
surface treatments must be utilized to achieve the desired piezoelectric response in ZnO nanowire devices.
surface treatments are required to eliminate polarization divergence and thus to achieve the desired enhancement of piezoelectric response in ZnO nanowire devices.

if one desires to utilize piezoelectric ZnO in a device application, then the surface must be treated to prevent surface polarization divergence and the device must be designed such that the ZnO nanowire has an axial orientation that is not prone to phase transformation.
